AccessionDate: The date when the specimen has been added to the collection
Barcodes.Methods.region: The region or locus of a gene that has been used to generate a RNA- or DNA-barcode from. Typical regions are: "COI", "ITS", "LSU", "SSU"
CollectingMethod: Name and short description of the method by which the specimen has been collected.
CollectionAgents.CollectorsName: The name(s) of one or more collectors of the specimen
CollectionDate: The date when the specimen has been collected.
CollectionHierarchyString: String representation of the collection hierarchy of an object. Collections are sorted by their organisational level and separated by ">"
CollectionName: Name of the collection where the object is stored
CollectionSpecimenID: The ID of the specimen (= sample) in the collection database.
CollectionsTree: Names and ids of the collections in the database.
CountryCache: The country of the specimen's collection site.
DatabaseAccronym: The accronym of the collection database that holds the data on a specimen.
FamilyCache: The taxonomic name of an organism at Family rank
Gender: The sex of the organism in the specimen part.
HabitatDescription: Information about the habitat from which the specimen has been collected.
IdentificationUnitID: The ID of an identified individual or object in the collection database.
ImagesAvailable: Flag if there is a media file available for the object.
LastIdentificationCache: The newest assignment of a scientific name to an object. Because of scientific progress names of species or other objects might change over the time. The names (identifications) given before are kept in the database. LastIdentificationCache holds the current most identification.
LifeStage: The life stage of the organism in the specimen part, e.g. "juvenil", "adult", "larva".
LocalityDescription: A more precise description of the locality where the specimen has been collected. For example the locality information given on a label of the collected object
LocalityVerbatim: A common name of the locality where the specimen has been collected, like "Loch Ness", "Badger's drift".
MatchedParentTaxa: The accepted taxonomic hierarchy of an object as is supported by curated taxonomies like GBIF backbone taxonomy or Catalog of Life. The field contains a list of taxon names at all ranks including the taxon in the MatchedTaxon field
MatchedSynonyms.Synonym: Known synonyms of the accepted name of an object collected from curated taxonomies like GBIF backbone taxonomy or Catalog of Life
MatchedTaxaHierarchyString: String representation of the taxonomic hierarchy of an object. Taxonomical names are sorted by their level and separated by ">".
MatchedTaxaTree: Names and ids of a taxonomic hierarchy of an object as is supported by curated taxonomies like GBIF backbone taxonomy or Catalog of Life
MatchedTaxaTree.Class: Taxon assigned to the object at the rank Class
MatchedTaxaTree.Family: Taxon assigned to the object at the rank Family
MatchedTaxaTree.Genus: Taxon assigned to the object at the rank Genus
MatchedTaxaTree.Order: Taxon assigned to the object at the rank Order
MatchedTaxaTree.Phylum: Taxon assigned to the object at the rank Phylum
MatchedTaxaTree.Regnum: Taxon assigned to the object at the rank Regnum
MatchedTaxaTree.Subclass: Taxon assigned to the object at the rank Subclass
MatchedTaxaTree.Subfamily: Taxon assigned to the object at the rank Subfamily
MatchedTaxaTree.Subgenus: Taxon assigned to the object at the rank Subgenus
MatchedTaxaTree.Suborder: Taxon assigned to the object at the rank Suborder
MatchedTaxaTree.Subphylum: Taxon assigned to the object at the rank Subphylum
MatchedTaxon: The accepted scientific name of an object as is supported by curated taxonomies like GBIF backbone taxonomy or Catalog of Life
MaterialCategory: The matierial type of the object in the collection, for example: microscopic slide, preserved specimen, bones, pelt. An object might only be observed and thus the material category would be "observed"
MediaTypes.MediaType: Types of media files associated with the object in the collection database.
NumberOfSpecimenImages: The number of images in the database depicting the object.
NumberOfUnits: The number of individual identified objects in the collected specimen.
OrderCache: The taxonomic name of an organism at Order rank
PartAccessionNumber: The accession number of a part of a collected specimen. Such a specimen part may contain individual objects from a collected specimen (e.g. organisms or minerals) or parts from the dissection of such objects (e.g. the leg of a spider). Specimen parts may hold several individuals or parts of them, but they must belong to the same specimen
Projects.Project: Projects in which the objects are used
SpecimenCreatedWhen: The date when the data of the specimen have been added to the database.
SpecimenPartID: The ID of a part of a specimen in the collection database
StableIdentifierURL: The URL refering to a specimen part in the collection database. It is composed of a base URL for each database and the ids in the tables CollectionSpecimen, IdentificationUnit, CollectionSpecimenPart
TypeStatus: When the identified organism is used as reference material for the formal description of a species. There are different kinds of types like Holotype, Syntype, Paratype.
VernacularTerms: Commonly used names of an object (e.g. species, mineral, or fossil) in different languages.
